# `sandloom.sdk.contracts`

Sync contracts: typed providers and callers, `contract_method` and its
helpers, and (advanced) the provider runtime.

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, Appendix C).

`from sandloom.sdk.contracts import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

## Beginner names

### `command`

```python
def command(
    *,
    idempotency_key: str,
    idempotency_scope: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    database: str | None = None,
    risk: Literal['money'] | None = None,
) -> Callable[[Callable[PS, R]], Callable[PS, R]]
```

Mark a provider method as a command: deduplicated by its
`idempotency_key` argument, committed in the provider's own unit, not
atomic with the caller (a saga step):

```python
@command(idempotency_key="operation_key")
async def reserve(self, amount: int, operation_key: str) -> int: ...
```

`risk="money"` declares a money source (ADR-0009).

### `Contract`

```python
def Contract(ref: ContractRef[P], *, optional: bool = False) -> P | OptionalContract[P]
```

The caller of contract `ref` (spec §5.3), declared at module level:

```python
quota = Contract(STATS_QUOTA_V1)          # required: startup fails without it
if not await quota.may_create_note(): ...
```

`define_module` adds it to the module's `consumes` (name and
`required` exact; `methods` from the direct `quota.<method>(` calls in
the defining module, else every method).

### `contract`

```python
def contract(name: str, *, database: str | None = None) -> Callable[[C], C]
```

Declare a stateless provider class of contract `name`:

```python
@contract("stats.quota.v1")
class Quota:
    async def may_create_note(self) -> bool: ...
```

Public `async def` methods are reads; `@command(...)` marks commands;
`@contract.read(planned=..., database=...)` keeps today's read options.

### `caller_user_id`

```python
def caller_user_id() -> UUID | None
```

The end user on whose behalf the running contract call executes, or
`None` (a system / service caller, a task, a consumer).

Locally the authenticated subject of the calling request; over RPC the
same subject, carried hop after hop in the signed caller facts of each
call's context (the provider binds them as its call's request scope). A
provider holds a personal resource to it (billing's personal spend,
Public API 1.0 spec §7.4).

### `contract_dto_problems`

```python
def contract_dto_problems(
    name: str,
    impl: Any,
    *,
    provider_module: str | None,
    module_packages: Iterable[str] = (),
    shared_packages: Iterable[str] = (),
) -> list[str]
```

DTOs of contract `name` no caller process could hold (SANDLOOM-C012).

A provider authors its contract DTOs (pydantic models, Enums) in its own
module package; `sandloom generate` copies each one a signature names
into the shared DTO package, where every caller imports the copy (the
stub names it, and a remote caller decodes into it). A DTO a module
package holds is therefore allowed in its OWN provider's signatures; what
no copy can come from is refused: a class of ANOTHER module's package
(use its generated copy from the shared DTO package), or one defined in a
function or `__main__`. Classes of a shared package (`sandloom.shared`,
`CONTRACT_DTO_PACKAGES`) are referenced as they are. The closed set of
DTO shapes is checked when `@contract` decorates the provider.

Checked only for contracts a MODULE registers (`provider_module` known);
kernel-level test registrations are exempt.


### `contract_method`

```python
def contract_method(
    fn: _F | None = None,
    *,
    command: bool = False,
    idempotency_key: str | None = None,
    idempotency_scope: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    database: str | None = None,
    planned: bool = False,
    risk: Literal['admin', 'money', 'security'] | None = None,
) -> _F | Callable[[_F], _F]
```

Mark an async method as a service-contract entry point.

Every call — local (`core.get_service`) or remote (internal RPC server) —
runs through `run_contract_call`: a command's `idempotency_key`
argument is required, and the
method body runs in the provider's own Unit of Work
(`contract_session`). Stack it UNDER `@classmethod`.

`command=True` commits the provider's UoW; such a call is NOT atomic with
the caller's transaction (saga semantics — the caller compensates or uses
events). `database` only applies to direct calls of an UNREGISTERED
provider (tests): a direct command call of a registered provider runs on
its registration's database under its contract name, sharing the
registry path's dedupe record.

`idempotency_scope` partitions a command's operation keys by named domain
arguments, for example `("tenant_type", "tenant_id")` for personal and
organization billing accounts. Changing this tuple changes the dedupe
namespace; retain domain UNIQUE operation keys when rolling out a change.

The signature must be wire-portable (checked when the provider is
registered): every parameter and the return annotated with a contract wire
type (`sandloom.core.contract_wire`), no `*args` / `**kwargs`.

`planned=True` (reads only) declares a contract whose body runs only
declared planner operations through `contract_reads`: no Unit of
Work is opened; the reads lease from the contract pool in a read-only
scope (`publish_event` / `record_audit` raise), with the tenant bound
exactly as for any contract call (the caller's locally, the verified RPC
context remotely).

`risk` (commands only) declares the risk of the command's effect at its
source, once (ADR-0009 item 7): `risk="money"` for a command that moves
money. It is recorded in the contract's describe document and snapshot;
a local call in a request records the effect there (its own
`idempotency_key` is its dedupe record), which triggers the automatic
audit row of a sensitive write.

### `contract_read_scope`

```python
def contract_read_scope(
    *,
    memo: bool | None = None,
    idle_ms: int | None = None,
) -> AsyncIterator[ContractReadScope]
```

Open a `ContractReadScope` for the block (reuses an outer one).

The framework opens one per HTTP request; open one explicitly in a
worker / script that makes several local read-contract calls in a row.
Memoisation is on unless `memo=False`; `idle_ms` defaults to
`CONTRACT_READ_SCOPE_IDLE_MS`, and `idle_ms < 0` holds the shared
connection until the block ends.

### `contract_reads`

```python
def contract_reads() -> Any
```

The declared-operations handle (`sandloom.core.orm.Reads`) of the running
contract call.

In a PLANNED read contract (`@contract_method(planned=True)`) the reads
run in the call's read-only scope on the provider's contract pool (one
shared read-only transaction for general-executor reads; the optimized
executor when enabled and eligible) — never in the caller's transaction,
locally and over RPC alike. In any other contract call they run on
`contract_session`. Under the test seam
(`bind_contract_session`) they run on the bound test session.

### `contract_schema`

```python
def contract_schema(impl: Any) -> ContractSchema
```

The validated `ContractSchema` of a contract provider (cached).

Every public member must be a `contract_method` with a
wire-portable signature, or a `ClassVar` constant (spec §5.3: never
exposed); private members (`_name`) are never exposed. Raises
`sandloom.core.contract_wire.ContractTypeError` listing every problem —
called at registration, so a non-portable contract never deploys.

### `ContractMethodRuntime`

```python
class ContractMethodRuntime(
    name: str,
    kind: Literal['read', 'command'],
    signature: inspect.Signature,
    annotations: dict[str, Any],
    returns: Any,
    idempotency_key: str | None = None,
    idempotency_scope: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    risk: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

The validated, wire-portable shape of one exposed contract method.

Built once at registration; the local path and the RPC server bind,
validate and encode every call through it, so both see the same argument
rules and the same result types.

#### `ContractMethodRuntime.describe`

```python
def describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]
```

JSON-able schema published by the RPC describe endpoint.

#### `ContractMethodRuntime.bind`

```python
def bind(
    self,
    label: str,
    args: Sequence[Any],
    kwargs: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    local: bool = False,
) -> tuple[tuple[Any, ...], dict[str, Any]]
```

Bind + validate UNTAGGED arguments exactly like a Python call would.

Returns `(positional_only_args, keyword_args)`. Unknown / missing
arguments, positional-only or keyword-only violations and values that
do not validate against their annotation raise
`ContractArgumentError` (422) before the provider runs.

`local=True` binds the caller's ORIGINAL values of an in-process
call: each goes through its parameter's `WirePlan` (immutable
exact-type values pass through, fully typed ones round-trip through
pydantic-core, the rest through the tagged tree) — what the provider
would receive over RPC.


Rebuild a result from its wire form using the return annotation.

### `ContractProvider`

```python
class ContractProvider(impl: Any, *, core: Any, database: str, name: str) -> None
```

A registered contract bound to its provider's core and database.

Returned by `core.get_service` for a locally provided contract and used
by the internal RPC server, so both paths run every call through
`run_contract_call`. Only the contract's exposed methods are visible
(exactly what a remote proxy can call); each local call is bound with
Python's rules, its arguments and result round-trip through the wire codec
and are validated against the annotations, and provider errors surface as
`ContractCallError` — so a local call is observably identical to a
remote one.


### `ContractReadScope`

```python
class ContractReadScope(*, memo: bool = True, idle_seconds: float | None = 0.0) -> None
```

A request-scoped scope in which LOCAL read-contract calls share work.

Opened per HTTP request by the framework (`ContractReadScopeMiddleware`)
or explicitly with `contract_read_scope`. Inside it:

* all local read-contract calls on the same database reuse ONE connection
  / transaction from the provider's contract pool (READ COMMITTED: every
  statement sees the latest committed data, exactly like a fresh UoW per
  call). It is NEVER the caller's transaction, so — as over RPC — the
  provider does not see the caller's uncommitted writes. It is always
  rolled back: when the scope ends, when a call raises or leaves ORM
  writes pending, and once the request stops making read calls —
  `idle_seconds=0` (default) releases it on the next event-loop turn
  after a call, i.e. as soon as the request awaits anything else, so
  back-to-back calls share it but it never idles in the pool's absence
  while the request does other I/O; `>0` keeps it that long; `None`
  holds it until the scope ends. A call that finds the shared connection
  busy (concurrent tasks, a read contract calling another on the same
  database) falls back to its own Unit of Work. A call that finds the
  shared transaction aborted by an earlier call's swallowed database
  error (SQLSTATE 25P02) drops that connection and reruns in its own
  Unit of Work (`stats["replaced"]`);
* identical read calls (local or RPC; same contract, method, bound tenant and
  arguments) are memoised for the rest of the scope — each caller still
  receives its own copy. Any command call (local or remote) clears the
  memo. External commits are visible after invalidation
  or in a new scope; use `memo=False` when every read must be fresh.

A read contract must not write: a raw DML statement it executed would be
visible to later read contracts of the same scope until rollback.

Run a read contract on the shared unit, or `_SCOPE_FALLBACK`.

#### `ContractReadScope.release_connections`

```python
async def release_connections(self) -> None
```

Roll back and release every shared connection NOW; the scope stays
usable (a later read reopens one). The operation-intent windows
(`external_call` / `release_check`) release it first (spec §4.6).

A read still running on a shared connection (another task) is waited
for, then its unit is closed: no read connection survives the drain.
A read that cannot finish first — the caller runs inside it — is
refused (SANDLOOM-R008) instead of waited for.

#### `ContractReadScope.aclose`

```python
async def aclose(self) -> None
```

End the scope: roll back and release every shared connection.

### `ContractRef`

```python
class ContractRef(Generic)(name: str, protocol: type[P] | None = None) -> None
```

A typed reference to a contract (emitted by the stub generator):
`STATS_QUOTA_V1: ContractRef[StatsQuotaV1] = ContractRef("stats.quota.v1",
StatsQuotaV1)`.

`protocol` is the stub's Protocol: a `Contract(REF)` caller receives
results as its methods' annotations name them (the generated DTO copies),
locally and over RPC. `None` (a hand-written reference): results as the
runtime returns them.

### `OptionalContract`

```python
class OptionalContract(Generic)(ref: ContractRef[P]) -> None
```

`Contract(REF, optional=True)`: `client()` is `None` only when the
provider is neither local nor bound in this deployment (decided at
startup); a deployed provider that is down still raises (503).

Use it only where the caller has a correct answer without the provider
(a feature off, an enrichment skipped); a gate whose absence must deny is
a required `Contract(REF)` (startup fails without it, SANDLOOM-B005).

### `run_contract_call`

```python
async def run_contract_call(
    func: Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]],
    args: tuple[Any, ...],
    kwargs: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    spec: ContractMethodSpec,
    core: Any = None,
    database: str = 'default',
    contract: str | None = None,
) -> Any
```

Run one contract call in the provider's own Unit of Work.

The single code path for local and RPC-served contract calls: enforces a
command's idempotency key and
deduplicates commands through the provider database's durable command log
(claimed and completed inside the command's own UoW), opens
the provider's UoW on `database` (rolled back for a read, committed +
outbox dispatched for a command) and exposes it via
`contract_session`. `contract` is the registered contract name (the
dedupe namespace; defaults to the method's qualified name).

### `service`

```python
def service(name: str, *, optional: bool = False) -> Any
```

The proxy of contract `name` (spec §2.3, §5.3).

`optional=True` returns `None` only when the provider is neither local
nor bound in this deployment; a deployed provider that is down still
raises when called.
